title: Make water safe by boiling
summary: Rolling boil for 1 minute, then cool and store covered. Boiling kills germs, not chemicals.

sources.title: CDC: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
EPA: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
CDC: Drinking Water Advisories: An Overview

blocks.text: Boiling is the surest way to kill viruses, bacteria and parasites. It is the first choice when you have fuel and a pot.

items: If the water is cloudy, let it settle and pour it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter first.
Bring the water to a **full rolling boil**.
Let it cool on its own. Don't add ice.
Store it in clean containers with tight lids.

blocks.text: Henrico is far below either altitude, so 1 minute applies. The two agencies give different altitude cut-offs. Both say 3 minutes when you're high up.

items: Flat taste: pour the water back and forth between two clean containers, or add a pinch of salt per quart or liter.
**Boil water that came through a filter or pitcher too.** Filters don't remove all germs.
Let boiled water cool before use so it doesn't burn anyone.
Boiling does **not** remove chemicals. Water contaminated with fuel or toxic chemicals can't be made safe by boiling. Use bottled water and call the health department.
Don't use untreated water for drinking, dishes, brushing teeth, washing food, making ice, or mixing baby formula.

blocks.text: Can't boil? Use bleach (30 minutes) or chlorine dioxide tablets instead. See those guides.
